question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(u,v)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-u-v &=-2 \\ -5u+6v &=-21\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $u.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $u$-coefficient in the first equation is $-1,$ while in the second equation it is $-5.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $-5,$ then the $u$-coefficient will become $5,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $-5$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}(\,-u-v &=-2\,)\,\times (-5) \\ -5u+6v &=-21\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}5u+5v &=10 \\ -5u+6v &=-21\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $u$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\cancel{5u}+5v & =10 \\ -\cancel{5u}+6v & =-21 \\ (5v+6v) & =(10-21) \\ 11v & =-11 \\ v & =-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $v=-1.$ However, we still need to find $u.$ To do this, we substitute $v=-1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-u-v & =-2 \\ -u-(-1) & =-2 \\ -u+1 & =-2 \\ -u & =-3 \\ u & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=3,\,v=-1,$ which can be expressed as $(3,-1).$

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(a,b)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}a-2b &=4 \\ 3a-4b &=10\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $a.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $a$-coefficient in the first equation is $1,$ while in the second equation it is $3.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $-3,$ then the $a$-coefficient will become $-3,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $3$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}(\,a-2b &=4\,)\,\times (-3) \\ 3a-4b &=10\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}-3a+6b &=-12 \\ 3a-4b &=10\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $a$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\cancel{3a}+6b & =-12 \\ \cancel{3a}-4b & =10 \\ (6b-4b) & =(-12+10) \\ 2b & =-2 \\ b & =-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $b=-1.$ However, we still need to find $a.$ To do this, we substitute $b=-1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}a-2b & =4 \\ a-2(-1) & =4 \\ a+2 & =4 \\ a & =2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=2,\,b=-1,$ which can be expressed as $(2,-1).$

\left\{\begin{aligned}8u-6v &=32 \\ -2u-v &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $u.$*

If we multiply the second equation by $4,$ then the $u$-coefficient will become $-8,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $8$ in the first equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}8u-6v &=32 \\ (\,-2u-v &=2\,)\,\times (4)\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}8u-6v &=32 \\ -8u-4v &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $u$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\cancel{8u}-6v & =32 \\ -\cancel{8u}-4v & =8 \\ (-6v-4v) & =(32+8) \\ -10v & =40 \\ v & =-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $v=-4.$ However, we still need to find $u.$ To do this, we substitute $v=-4$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}8u-6v & =32 \\ 8u-6(-4) & =32 \\ 8u+24 & =32 \\ 8u & =8 \\ u & =1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=1,\,v=-4,$ which can be expressed as $(1,-4).$

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-9x-7y &=6 \\ 3x+y &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $x.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $x$-coefficient in the first equation is $-9,$ while in the second equation it is $3.$ 

If we multiply the second equation by $3,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $9,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $-9$ in the first equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-9x-7y &=6 \\ (\,3x+y &=-6\,)\,\times (3)\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}-9x-7y &=6 \\ 9x+3y &=-18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\cancel{9x}-7y & =6 \\ \cancel{9x}+3y & =-18 \\ (-7y+3y) & =(6-18) \\ -4y & =-12 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=3.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=3$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-9x-7y & =6 \\ -9x-7(3) & =6 \\ -9x-21 & =6 \\ -9x & =27 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-3,\,y=3,$ which can be expressed as $(-3,3).$
